messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the host driver bump to 549.70 on the eu-west pool we're seeing a ~10-18% p95 latency regression for short sequences (<=64) and a weird drop in KV cache hit rate.
maria: Quick numbers from the last 30m: p50 ~1% up, p95 +12%, tail errors stable. KV hit rate went from 92% -> 58% on short-seq routes.
alex: Yikes. Did autotuner change the kernel picks? Last time that hit rate / latency combo correlated with kernel swap for short seq.
maria: Yep — the selector logs show a different kernel now for many shortseq requests. Example from a runtime probe:

```
[selector] model:redwood-7b seq:32 batch:4 hw:V100 driver:549.70 -> pick: attn_slow_loop (cost: 1.12) tie_score:0.02
[selector] previous_best: attn_vec_fast (cost: 0.98) tie_score: -0.05
```

maria: The autotuner seems to prefer attn_slow_loop post-driver-bump.
sam: Can you paste a tiny perf trace (nvprof / nsys aggregate) for the two kernels? shortseq, batch=4, kvcache on vs off please.
maria: Pasted low-res flame for same workload (shortened):

```
-- attn_vec_fast (old driver)
gpu_util: 72% | kernel_time: 0.42ms | mem_copy: 0.05ms
kv_hit: 0.92
-- attn_slow_loop (new driver)
gpu_util: 61% | kernel_time: 0.68ms | mem_copy: 0.09ms
kv_hit: 0.59
```

maria: Notice the higher kernel_time and increased memory copy fraction — explains latency and KV hit drop (more time spent reloading KV slices).
devon: Immediate mitigation options:
- pin driver back on a canary set of nodes
- override kernel pick with selector env to prefer attn_vec_fast for seq<=64
- tighten batching (reduce latency window) so we avoid the path that triggers attn_slow_loop

alex: For rollout: canary 5% traffic on eu-west (20 hosts). If stable for 30m promote. Ops, can you prepare an image with driver 543.67 and a flag to force kernel override?
ops-bot: @ops-bot starting canary provisioning: creating host group rwi-eu-west-canary-1 (20 hosts). ETA ~ 8m :hourglass:
ops-bot: Canary image will be driver:543.67, runtime:2026-03-16. Will attach label:driver-pin=543.67

sam: To force kernel in runtime for immediate soft-fix add ENV:
```
RW_KERNEL_PREFER=attn_vec_fast
RW_KERNEL_TIEBREAK=prefer_vectorized
```
alex: Also add route-level override as temporary config (example route patch):
```
PATCH /routes/shortseq
{
  "kernel_override": "attn_vec_fast",
  "batching": {"max_latency_ms": 2}
}
```

devon: Another quick mitigation: disable KV prefetch for short sequences. We saw prefetch cause more memcpy thrash on the new driver. Example config change:
```
route.shortseq.kv_cache.prefetch=false
```

maria: I ran a local repro harness with `--seed 42 --seq 32 --batch 4` and the regression reproduces locally under containerized NV driver 549.70. I can push the harness to ci/perf with a small job.
sam: Good — please push. We need a deterministic e2e perf test to gate the rollback. Add telemetry that logs selector decision diffs:
```
selector_event: {model, seq_len, batch_size, picked_kernel, candidate_score, driver_version}
```

alex: Long-term fix ideas:
- tighten selector tie-breaker: prefer vectorized kernels for seq<=64 and batch_size<=8 unless the candidate score delta > 0.15
- add driver-aware kernel calibration step in autotuner (re-run microbench on driver upgrade)
- prefer kernel with lower memcpy fraction for KV-enabled routes

devon: Action items (short):
1) ops: start canary with pinned driver (auth: @ops-bot) — in progress
2) infra: deploy runtime env override RW_KERNEL_PREFER on all eu-west frontends (sam + devon)
3) dev: push perf harness + selector telemetry (maria)
4) perf: run canary traffic, gather p95 & kv_hit, rollback if kv_hit < 85% or p95 reg > 7% sustained for 10m (alex)

deploy-bot: Canary group rwi-eu-west-canary-1 created. Traffic slice: 5% assigned. Canary start: 1768007400
ops-bot: Driver-pin image pushed to canary hosts. Starting healthcheck loop.

maria: I'll keep monitoring selector_event logs. If we see attn_slow_loop still winning on the pinned driver we need to dig deeper into the kernel's memory ordering assumptions.
alex: If canary is green at +30m we'll rollback EU-west fleet to pinned driver and schedule a follow-up postmortem. If it's flaky we'll revert kernel selector in runtime as the safer fallback.
sam: Also add a quick redispatch script to move warm KV shards away from hosts running 549.70 to reduce cold loads during the canary.

devon: Noting postmortem owners: maria (debug), sam (telemetry + perf test), alex (rollback decision), ops-bot (canary roll)
maria: Thanks team. Will post perf graphs in here in 10m. :eyes:
